Debase

/dih-BAYS/ - rhymes with erase · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Debase means to lower the quality or esteem of something.

Selling knighthoods to anyone with the fee debased an honor that soldiers had bled for.

Worked Example

A publicist can now call a sandwich epic, a parking spot epic, a Tuesday epic. Reviewers who reached for the word in 1950 meant Homer and thousand-page sagas; by now it has been spent on so little that it buys almost nothing. Grand words work that way: apply one to small things often enough and the grandness drains out of it for everyone.

Debase is the exact word for what happened to it, because debase means to lower the quality or esteem of something — the word still exists, still gets said everywhere, but it stands for less. Cheapen comes close, yet cheapen often stops at price or shine; debase reaches the worth underneath, the respect a thing can command.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

devalue: Devalue is the ledger's word: it lowers what something is worth in money or measurable terms — a currency, a stock, a house. Debase cuts deeper than any price tag, draining the esteem a thing commands, so a debased honor can cost nothing and still have lost everything.

water down: To water down a thing is to weaken it by dilution — a watered-down rule or drink still exists, only thinner and fainter. Debase passes a harsher judgment: the thing is not merely weaker but lowered, worth less in quality and in everyone's esteem.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

elevate: raise in worth or standing

ennoble: lift a thing into dignity

Where it sits · how deeply the value is damaged — cheapen → debase → ruin

cheapen vs. debase: Cheapen is far milder than debase — a tacky ad can cheapen a brand for a season without changing what the product is; to debase it is to lower the real worth underneath.

ruin vs. debase: Ruin goes further than debase — a debased honor still gets awarded, just respected less; a ruined one no one will accept at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: down

Root — base

Root — base: low (Old French bas)

Put it together

Put it together: De- (down) + base (low) = to drive down toward the low. English built the word at home in the 1500s: base was then an everyday adjective for "low, lowly" — a base motive, base metal — and debasing something pushes it down into that company.

Use the root in a new word: bass

Use the root in a new word: bass: The bass part in a choir is literally the low part — Italian basso, from the same Latin bassus, "low," behind base.

Word Choice

formal / critical

Debase is for worth: honors, prizes, words, currencies. When a person's dignity is the target, this unit's demean is the word; when a surface is spoiled, deface; when something clean is made impure, defile. Cheapen is the everyday stand-in, but it gossips about price where debase judges value.
